Rule A already divides by a combination of kinetic constants. The coefficient of the constant term, d0, has the units of every other coefficient times a concentration power, so every term of D/d0 is dimensionless as a whole. For steady-state uni-uni, d0 = k_ES_to_E_S + k_ES_to_E_P and the S term becomes S·k_E_S_to_ES/(k_ES_to_E_S + k_ES_to_E_P) = S/Km. I checked the units on all 757 laws that have a constant term. For steady-state ordered bi-bi, D/d0 is exactly Cleland's eleven terms, 1 + A/Kia + Ka·B/(Kia·Kb) + … .

The 49 laws without a constant term (ping-pong) cannot show a leading 1 unless you divide by a concentration. Every term holds a concentration, and every metabolite is missing from some term, so dividing by any concentration puts a 1/A somewhere (Dalziel's form, NaN at A = 0).

They can still be made dimensionless. Divide by a virtual constant term: the combination of coefficients that has a constant term's units, N = c(A)·c(B)/c(AB) for a bi-bi ping-pong. With products at zero, classic ping-pong prints a + b + a·b, with a = A/Ka and b = B/Kb: no 1, no division by a concentration.

- Cleland's choice of N, built from the substrate-saturation terms, covers 40 of the 49.
- A general construction (affinely independent terms, substrates first) covers 8 of the other 9, about 40 lines.
- The last one, handwritten/21, depends only on B/P, so no dimensionless form exists; it keeps the plain coefficient division.

Two caveats:

- Many dimensionless groups still carry a ratio of constants as their coefficient, such as Kia/Ka on A·B in ordered bi-bi (618 of the 757). Those belong to the mechanism, not to the normalization.
- Printing clean Km's needs cancellation of common polynomial factors. That affects only the display.

I added this as a new option on the card.

Follow-up on the compact form: yes, and it has a classic precedent, Cleland's coefficient form (num1·A·B − num2·P·Q over constant + coef_A·A + …). I would print it as a second form next to the full law:

v = E_total·n_0·(A·B − P·Q/Keq) / (1 + d_A·A + d_B·B + d_A_B·A·B + d_P·P + …)

followed by one legend line per coefficient (d_A = …) in the fitted constants. Three suggestions:

- Name each coefficient by what it multiplies (d_A_B multiplies A·B) rather than numbering it. The name then says what it is, and it does not change when terms are added or reordered.
- Keep the Haldane factor in the numerator, (ΠS − ΠP/Keq) times a positive polynomial, so Keq stays visible.
- Say in the legend that the coefficients are functions of the fitted constants, not parameters: they are tied to each other (ordered bi-bi has 12 coefficient ratios at rank 7).

It reuses the coefficients the normalization already computes, so it costs about 25–30 lines of printer code. Allosteric laws print it per conformation. I put it on a new card, C10.
